title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-grace-lee
content:
Account: NimbusPay (target: mid-market fintech / payments orchestration)
Primary goals: reduce per-transaction inference latency for fraud scoring, keep RAG/PII data private, cut per-transaction cost as volume scales.
Background notes:
- Nimbus is a payments platform for SMBs in NA/EU; raised Series B 2024, expanding merchant onboarding.
- Current infra: homegrown scoring service + vendor ML model (closed). They call it "score-v2"; suspicious high tail latency during peak auth spikes.
- Security: SOC2 + PCI readiness in progress. They prefer VPC or customer-managed key options.
- Decision timeline: exploring vendors for Q2 2026 procurement; procurement + security signoff tends to take 6-8 weeks.
- Key stakeholders (based on LinkedIn + discovery call):
  - VP Infra: Jordan Matthews (procurement + infra budget owner)
  - Head of ML/Models: Priya Shah (model ops & quality)
  - Security Lead: Marcus Hall (compliance, KMS/HSM)
  - Product lead (merchant onboarding): Lena Rodriguez (product metrics owner)

Pain points / Signals:
- Latency tail > 300ms at 95th during spikes -> losing merchant approvals / throughput.
- Current vendor costs scale poorly with volume; ops team spending time tuning batching.
- Concern about vendor lock-in + lack of private deployment options for sensitive PII flows.

Why Redwood could fit:
- Dedicated capacity: predictable throughput and SLA for low tail latency (sell: predictable 95th/99th guarantees).
- Private deployment: VPC + on-prem packaging for PCI-sensitive flows + KMS/HSM integrations for keys.
- Optimize recommendations: batching + KV cache for prefix patterns in scoring -> clear unit-cost reductions.
- Observable rollout: per-route latency/cost dashboards to track regressions during model changes.

Outbound email (cold) - short variant:
Subject: Cut fraud-scoring latency + cost for NimbusPay
Hi Jordan — quick intro, I’m Grace on Partnerships at Redwood Inference. We help payments platforms keep authorization latency predictable while lowering per-transaction ML costs (we run customer-grade LLM inference in VPCs / dedicated pools).
Noticed NimbusPay has latency spikes during peak auth windows — would love 20 min to share a few concrete levers (dedicated pools + batching + KV cache) that have reduced tail latency 30-50% for similar customers.
Are you open to a quick call next week?
Best,
Grace

Follow-up / multi-touch sequence (skeleton):
- Day 0: Cold email (short variant)
- Day 3: Short note with one-pager link + a 1-2 line case study (e.g., "Cut 95th tail 40% for PayFlowX")
- Day 7: DM on LinkedIn to VP Infra (personalized line referencing blog/case study)
- Day 14: Final push — ask for intro to ML owner if non-responsive

LinkedIn DM template:
Hi Jordan, I posted a short note on latency strategies for payment auth flows — thought it might be relevant. Happy to share a quick audit of 1-2 low-hanging config changes we usually recommend (no infra changes required).

Discovery call framework (20 min):
- 0-5: intros + quick context (confirm decision timeline + stakeholders)
- 5-10: current infra + pain (latency numbers, batch patterns, model variants, peak QPS)
- 10-15: quick architecture sketch of Redwood options (hosted -> dedicated -> private) + cost levers (batching, KV cache, quantization)
- 15-18: compliance/security questions (KMS, SOC2, PCI gaps)
- 18-20: next steps: offer a short tech audit + sample perf run / POC ops (2-4 weeks)

Common objections & concise responses (use in slack / quick replies)
- "We build this in-house":
  Response: totally makes sense — we aren’t trying to replace model development. We sit as an inference runtime layer + orchestration: keep your model weights, get predictable latency/cost + fallbacks. Also helps ops reduce time tuning batching.
- "Cost — vendor is more expensive":
  Response: short calc: we look at cost-per-token / per-inference + tail latency cost (lost approvals). With batching + cache + dedicated pools, net unit cost often drops 20-40% at scale for scoring workloads. Happy to share an anonymized TCO slide.
- "Security / PCI concerns":
  Response: Redwood Private supports VPC control plane + KMS/HSM integration; we can run in-customer VPC or an on-prem package for air-gapped flows. Offer to loop security for architecture review.
- "Lock-in / migration friction":
  Response: we support standard model formats and offer phased rollouts + read-only shadowing to compare outputs before taking production traffic. Rollouts + automatic fallback make rollback low-friction.

Quick POC idea (2-4 weeks):
- Week 0: kickoff + access to sample scoring endpoint / model artifact (or we shadow call)
- Week 1: baseline perf metrics (95th/99th latency) + small config experiment (batcher + KV cache)
- Week 2: run dedicated pool baseline with sample traffic -> measure tail + cost delta
- Week 3: security review + demo to stakeholders
- Deliverable: perf report + recommended config + TCO estimate

Open questions / TODOs (for internal):
- Does Priya prefer vendor-managed models or customer-owned artifacts? (ask on intro)
- Get benchmark deck: need 95/99 latency baselines, QPS distribution, payload sizes
- Prep anonymized case study: "payments auth: reduced 95th tail 40% + 30% cost savings" (ask growth for permission)
- Ask Solutions Eng for a short script to simulate bursty auth traffic (QPS pattern)

Notes to self (shorthand):
- If Jordan is procurement-heavy, lead with SLA + dedicated capacity pricing (monthly), then move to security.
- If Priya is paranoid about drift/regression, emphasize Redwood Optimize evaluations + per-rollout quality monitoring.
- Use "no infra changes" messaging only when true for POC; otherwise be explicit about minimal runtime integration steps.

Potential next-step email (after discovery):
Subject: NimbusPay — 2-week perf audit + POC plan
Jordan / Team — thanks for your time today. Based on our convo, propose a short perf audit + POC to quantify latency tail and cost levers. High-level plan attached and a list of access items we’ll need. Would Wed/Thu next week work for a kickoff?

-- end scratch notes --
